purpose: Formative retrieval or application practice where one or more questions have objectively defensible correct answers and feedback is intended to strengthen understanding or performance.
learningRationale: Use after relevant instruction or context to require retrieval, discrimination or application. Feedback should explain why an answer is appropriate rather than merely marking it correct or incorrect.
useWhen: A learner should retrieve or apply knowledge before continuing.
The response can be judged against a defensible correct answer.
Immediate explanatory feedback will improve understanding or transfer.
avoidWhen: The prompt is reflective and has no correct answer; use a Reflection component.
The choice represents a nuanced workplace judgement with branching consequences; use a Decision Point or scenario component.
Interaction is being added only to vary presentation.

variants.name: Knowledge Check — Single
variants.description: One formative question with immediate feedback.

variants.name: Knowledge Check — Sequence
variants.description: A short set of formative questions using the same question contract and optional guided progression.

accessibility: Use a fieldset and legend for each question.
Use native radio buttons or checkboxes; do not recreate selection controls with divs.
Feedback is associated through aria-describedby and announced through role=status with aria-live=polite.
Focus remains predictable after answer checking; sequence navigation moves focus to the newly active question heading or control.
Visible focus styling is supplied by the shared ISQ design system.
Feedback does not rely on colour alone.
Touch targets must remain usable at mobile widths.
No essential information depends on animation.
keyboardBehaviour: Native radio/checkbox keyboard behaviour is retained. Buttons activate with native keyboard behaviour. Sequence navigation must not trap focus.
responsiveBehaviour: Question options stack naturally. Sequence navigation must remain readable and operable at narrow widths without horizontal dependence.

javascript.deployment: For Rise candidate deployments, use one governed copy of the controller per block. Do not fork or independently edit controller logic in courses.
javascript.telemetry: Optional. Emits isq:knowledge-check-answered. No LRS transport is embedded.

riseConstraints: The component runs inside the Rise custom-code iframe and must not assume control of the parent page.
Course-specific IDs must be supplied per implementation when telemetry is enabled.
Do not embed LRS credentials in the block.
The learner interaction remains functional when no telemetry adapter is available.
qaRequiredBeforeApproval: Screen-reader semantics and feedback announcement pass
xAPI adapter review with ISQ xAPI governance stakeholder
